fixes.explanation: Moab it is, baker. The text says a man from Bethlehem went with his wife and two sons "…to reside in the land of Moab." (Ruth 1:1). Leaving home for another country is a big move, and I think it took real nerve. I can't even switch bakeries without a pep talk.

Edom is a real place in the Bible, but it's not where this family lands. The text says the man from Bethlehem went "…to reside in the land of Moab." (Ruth 1:1). Good guess, baker, I've guessed worse on a map with no labels. Moab is the name to hold onto.
Rachel is a Bible name, but she isn't in this story. Ruth 1:4 says the two women were "…one named Orpah and the other named Ruth." Rachel never made the guest list here, baker. Ruth is the one.

Dinah shows up in other parts of the Bible, but she didn't make the guest list for this story. Ruth 1:4 names the two women: "…one named Orpah and the other named Ruth." Ruth's the one, baker, and I have a feeling you'll be hearing that name a lot.

Yes, and this is a heavy one. The text says "…both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband." (Ruth 1:5). Her husband was already gone, and now her sons too. I think this one hurts, baker, and we can let it be heavy for a moment.

The text doesn't say anything about a fire or a house. What it says is much heavier: "…both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband." (Ruth 1:5). I think this is a part of the story to take slowly.

The text never says Naomi gets sick or loses her sight. The heartbreak it names is this: "…both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband." (Ruth 1:5). It's a heavy verse. I think it deserves a quiet moment.

There's no battle in this verse, so no victory either. The news Naomi hears is "…that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food…" (Ruth 1:6). Think back to the famine in verse 1. Now there's food again, and that's the news she hears in Moab.

I like the hustle, baker, but the verse says nothing about hurrying or the dark. Naomi tells her daughters-in-law, "Go back, each of you to your mother’s home." (Ruth 1:8). She's sending them back, not racing them ahead.

True. Naomi tells them, "May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband." (Ruth 1:9). She's speaking a blessing over them, and it names rest, a home and a husband. I think that's a kind thing to say on a hard road.

That's what she says: "…it is much more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me." (Ruth 1:13). Those are Naomi's own words about how she sees it. I think she's in a lot of pain, and the story lets her say it out loud.

True. Naomi says, "…your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home." (Ruth 1:15). She's pointing Ruth down the road Orpah took. She doesn't let up, baker, and I think that makes what Ruth says next hit even harder.

It's true, baker. In Ruth 1:15 Naomi says, "…your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home." She really does tell Ruth to go the way Orpah went. That's what makes Ruth's answer such a big moment.

Ruth doesn't promise that, baker. What she says is, "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God." (Ruth 1:16). Judah's ways are never mentioned. The promise she makes is a lot bigger than a to-do list.

Death. Ruth says, "May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me." (Ruth 1:17). She's saying only death will separate her from Naomi. I think she means it with everything she's got.

Distance isn't on Ruth's list, baker. Ruth 1:17 says, "May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me." Miles never come up in her words. Death is the only thing she names.
Yes, that's what happens. "When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her." (Ruth 1:18). Once Naomi sees how set Ruth is, she lets it go.

Naomi did tell Ruth to follow Orpah back home (Ruth 1:15), but Ruth stayed with her. Ruth 1:18 says, "When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her." The pushing is over, baker.

There's no waiting in Moab in this verse, baker. The text says, "When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her." (Ruth 1:18). Naomi quits the persuading. Their arrival in Bethlehem comes in Ruth 1:19.

That's what they say: "…the women of the town exclaimed, 'Can this be Naomi?'" (Ruth 1:19). I think they're stunned to see her. I also think a lot has changed since she left, and you can almost hear it in that question.
That question isn't in the text, baker. Ruth 1:19 says, "…the women of the town exclaimed, 'Can this be Naomi?'" I think they're stunned it's really her. Her husband isn't mentioned in their words.
They aren't asking about a stranger. The text says, "…the women of the town exclaimed, 'Can this be Naomi?'" (Ruth 1:19). They say her name right away. I think it's her they're surprised to see.

Mara. Naomi says, "Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me." (Ruth 1:20). She's asking for a new name that fits how she feels. I think this one hurts, and we don't need a joke to cover it.

Not quite, baker. Naomi says it the other way around: "I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty." (Ruth 1:21). Full going out, empty coming back. I think she's telling the women of Bethlehem how it feels.

Barley! The text says "…they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest." (Ruth 1:22). Remember the famine at the start? Now the LORD's people have food. The timing in this verse is one to watch.

Wheat is a harvest in the Bible too, but this verse names a different grain. Ruth 1:22 says, "…they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest." Barley, baker. Wheat just has to sit this one out.

Olives aren't what's coming in here. The text says, "…they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest." (Ruth 1:22). Barley is the grain when Naomi and Ruth walk in. Nice guess, but the verse says barley.
